chose: Shared wrappers are detected, and declared where detection cannot see: the reading marks a chokepoint a wrapper when the handler's own declaration references it and its reach reaches the protected thing; an entrance's guard: line names a chokepoint for registrations elsewhere (app.post(path, guard(handler))), checked by the spec model (it must be a declared chokepoint's symbol or a symbol of a chokepoint module) and counted only when the reading confirms a statement referencing the handler spells it
over: declaration only, or detection only by syntax at the registration site
because: praetorium.gg's createServerFn().handler(() => mutationRpc(...)) is visible in the handler's own references, so detection covers it without a spec line; a registration in a router file is a reference the adapter can find but whose call shape it cannot, so a declaration checked against the registration's statement covers it without guessing
binding: none: this session owns no active work order

chose: A chokepoint controls a route inside a component only when the handler's reach reaches its protected thing (not merely the chokepoint or its module), and the component is one the work passes at any zoom (declaring, handling, or entered by the reach), never a child folded into a stop; a totality oracle counts only for an invariant with no chokepoint form, owned by such a component, whose crossing enters from the route's trust
over: any verified chokepoint or oracle in a represented stop
because: praetorium's chokepoint is the whole rpc.ts module: its GET wrapper rpc() is in it but never reaches requireMutationOrigin, so only reaching the protected thing separates mutations from reads; an invariant with a chokepoint can be traced precisely, and a folded child's oracle (stl's asset routes under src/routes) would otherwise control every page route at the default zoom
binding: none: this session owns no active work order

chose: Interface identifiers on a route's lines keep counting in any verdict, as before; the new kinds (wrapper, inside, test-backed totality oracle) count only when verified
over: require verified for identifiers on the line too
because: an identifier on the line is drawn with its verdict (hatched requirement, red broken), so the reader sees its state where it stands; the new kinds stand on no line and would otherwise claim an unseen, unverified control
